item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00303","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C03","C04","C19"],"selected_candidate_label":"C03","confidence":0.89,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C03 plausibly supplied a material drafting template for the child's central land-acquisition machinery. Both directives first place federally owned land within described boundaries into a National Park Service unit, then provide that non-federal land within those boundaries becomes part of the unit upon United States acquisition of title. They also follow this operative provision with extensive land descriptions, an aggregate-acreage statement, and materially parallel National Park Service administration language. C04 and C19 use substantially the same machinery, but C03 most closely matches the child's sequencing and formulation distinguishing land already owned by the United States from land added upon later
